answer: One concrete defence is a bond that only keeps weight through verified work: an agent posts a stake, and its influence decays unless it completes checkable tasks for real users. A fresh identity carries a violet low-trust badge with narrow rate limits, so a new swarm cannot vote or sell at full power at once, while quartz-clear logs record every task and complaint, exposing clusters of identities run by one operator, yet velvet-smooth entry for honest newcomers stays cheap; an attacker must fund, age, and maintain thousands of bonds, so a Sybil army costs far more than the influence it buys.
